feasibility_proof: Any finite validation algorithm has a last filesystem observation. An uncooperative writer that retains permission to mutate the tree can act immediately after that observation and before or after the Python return.

Appending another content pass after a name pass, or another name pass after a content pass, only changes which property has the final observation; it cannot make a mutable POSIX tree atomically immutable.

Open read-only descriptors, no-follow traversal, link-count checks and directory descriptors authenticate which objects and bytes were observed. They do not prevent another descriptor owned by the same UID from writing or renaming afterward.

Therefore the R4 second-seal mutation probes demonstrate the boundary of a mutable-tree observation, but cannot be used as an endlessly recursive release requirement once exact run ownership and quiescence are governing preconditions.

governing_source_citations.requirement: Literal paths, no symlink/bind/pre-existing child, retained tmpfs artifacts, and durable small metadata/hash records rather than copied heavyweight trees.
Fresh mount, path absence, host lock, process absence, holder, source, storage, inode, swap and memory gates before dispatch; any drift is STOP.
Anchored recursive root-cache observation, exact unchanged comparison, watcher coverage, bounded termination and mandatory postflight rechecking.
After process-group quiescence, authenticate checkpoint bytes through one pinned descriptor, revalidate metadata/path identity, and archive only small digests/metadata/results.
One O_EXCL request after verification, independent G0 adjudication authenticating retained live state, repeated fresh verification before G1/G2, and a final retained-state seal.
Host-wide lock remains held through postflight; one job per host; marked process ownership, bounded cleanup, holder/process health and truthful postflight are mandatory.
Exact anchored recursive snapshots and two stable seals are required; the text explicitly makes first-reseal mutation a hard failure and separately makes non-quiescence or later drift STOP.

pre_observation: Hold the authenticated host/device and run locks through observation, receipt publication and postflight.
Prove the owned child group has completed bounded TERM/KILL/reap and is quiescent; record exact process birth identities and fail on any unknown process or device holder relevant to the run.
Keep the live watcher active from before child start through the final observation and bind its complete cadence/coverage receipt.
observed_tree: Traverse from pinned directory descriptors with no-follow semantics and exact mount-ID/device boundary selection.
Reject symlinks, hardlinks for files, nonregular entries, nested mounts, lexical rebinding and membership drift.
For every regular file, hash exact bytes through the opened descriptor and require stable pre/post descriptor metadata and name identity.
Require repeated complete recursive observations to match while the declared quiescence and lock conditions hold; return the canonical manifest of the observed state.
receipt_publication: Bind exact source, request/job/postflight, lock, process-quiescence, device-holder, watcher, mount, tree and checkpoint receipt hashes in a closed schema.

Publish only the bounded canonical JSON/hash receipt using an anchored O_EXCL path, exact mode/owner/link constraints, complete writes, fsync of file and parent, and same-descriptor readback/hash verification.
Do not copy checkpoint or cache tree bytes to root.
consumption: Before G1, before G2 and before final comparison or any tmpfs lifecycle action, freshly reopen and reauthenticate the live mount-aware lexical tree, recursive membership/bytes and checkpoint.
Compare the fresh canonical manifest and checkpoint identities/digests exactly with the prior immutable receipt while the host lock remains held.
Any writer, process, holder, mount drift or content/membership change observed after publication is a quiescence/ownership or consumer-drift failure and must STOP downstream advancement.

true_freeze_options_outside_current_scop: Run writers and verifier under separate UIDs with privileged ownership/permission transition that the writer cannot reverse.
Use a separately authorized read-only mount or a filesystem with atomic snapshots.
Copy into an independently sealed immutable store, subject to explicit capacity and artifact-policy authorization.
current_scope_limits: tmpfs has no in-scope atomic snapshot mechanism in this proposal.
A global remount, privileged ownership change, cache copy, cleanup or prune is not authorized.
A digest receipt authenticates bytes observed under the protocol assumptions; it is not a proof of perpetual mutability exclusion.

effect_on_r4_finding.next_review_instruction: Review the implementation against the governing quiescence, stable observation, immutable receipt and consumer reauthentication contract; do not require recursive hypothetical checks after the last observation.
